html:
A siege of Constantinople by the Ottoman sultan Murad II in the summer of 1422.

When Murad came to the throne in 1421, the Byzantines under Manuel II and his son John VIII backed a rival claimant, Mustafa, against him. Murad beat Mustafa and then turned on the city to punish it. He brought cannon and built earthworks before the land walls.

A great assault in August failed. The defenders credited the Virgin Mary, said to have appeared on the walls. Soon after, a revolt led by Murad's young brother, also backed by Byzantium, drew him back to Anatolia, and he lifted the siege. The same year he also put Thessalonica under siege. In 1424 the Byzantines made peace and agreed to pay tribute.
sum: A siege of Constantinople by the Ottoman sultan Murad II in the summer of 1422.
